title: Shadow surge control and tenant quarantine for mirrored traffic
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a production-safe shadow/mirroring pipeline enhancement that prevents cost and reliability surprises by applying tenant-aware surge control, quarantine gating, adaptive sampling, and automatic rollback triggers. This ticket covers the runtime and control-plane changes required to safely duplicate live requests for model lifecycle activities (validation, quality checks, comparison telemetry) while guaranteeing tenant isolation and cost budgets.

Scope:
- Shadow duplication remains side-effect free (no responses returned to clients).
- Introduce per-tenant mirrored traffic budgets and dynamic sampling policies (steady-state rate + burst reservoir).
- Implement a quarantine path for tenants that exceed error or cost thresholds; quarantined tenants have their mirrored traffic either rate-limited or stopped while production traffic continues.
- Add cost accounting tags for mirrored requests so billing/usage surfaces and alerts distinguish mirrored tokens from production tokens.
- Wire auto-rollback signals into rollout controller: regressions from mirrored metrics (latency, error-rate, hallucination alerts, QA mismatch) can mark a canary as failed.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change production routing or fallback policies for live inference (only mirrored path).
- Does not implement new user-facing UI in Console; will emit metrics and flags for Console work in a follow-up PM ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Mirrored traffic is sampled by tenant with two configurable knobs: steady-rate (tokens/min) and burst-reservoir (tokens).
When a tenant exceeds its mirrored cost budget for the billing period, mirrored requests for that tenant throttle to 0% and an alert is generated to infra-safety.
Quarantine flow isolates mirrored execution to dedicated queues and nodes that enforce KV-cache scoping so no tenant KV/cache leakage occurs.
Mirrored requests are annotated with billing tags and are visible in existing token-cost dashboards with separate breakdowns for mirrored vs production tokens.

Auto-rollback pipeline consumes mirrored-derived signals (latency p95 increase > 50ms, error-rate > 2% absolute, QA-set mismatch > 1%) and triggers a canary rollback event in the rollout controller within 2 minutes of detection.
E2E test harness validates side-effect-freedom by ensuring duplicated HTTP requests to shadow services do not alter external systems (DB write counts remain unchanged).
Performance regression: mirrored path should add no more than 2% additional latency to the gateway selection path when sampling is enabled (measured in staged load tests).
progress_updates: 2026-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Ticket created after incident post-mirrored-run where unexpected traffic doubled token spend for a single tenant. Added initial scope and non-goals.

2026-02-23 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype of adaptive sampler implemented (probabilistic steady-rate + reservoir for bursts). Benchmarked token savings vs naive 100% mirror: ~86% token reduction on average across sampled tenants.

2026-02-28 - SRE review: Raised concerns about KV-cache isolation. Decided to run mirrored requests on separate runtime queues with explicit cache namespace. SRE opened ENG-27615 to add cache-namespace enforcement in runtime.

2026-03-04 - Marco Ruiz: Added billing tag header X-RW-MIRROR=true and updated ingestion pipeline to classify mirrored tokens for charge and metric segmentation. Filed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5124

2026-03-07 - QA: Implemented e2e harness that replays production traffic to mirrored path and asserts no DB mutations; found one legacy endpoint that performed a metrics increment — patched in https://github.com/redwood-inference/services/pull/2238

2026-03-10 - Stakeholder sync: PM and Console teams asked for the mirrored-cost metric to be exported to Console; created follow-up PM ticket PM-489 to surface mirrored cost and quarantine state in UI.
decisions: Use tenant-scoped token budgets (monthly) instead of raw request counts because token usage aligns with billing and cost control objectives.

Adaptive sampler algorithm: reservoir sampling with exponential decay window to allow short bursts without blowing steady-state budget. This balances fidelity during spikes with long-run cost controls.

Quarantine path runs on a separate priority lane with compute isolated from production inference to prevent noisy neighbor effects; mirrored tasks are pinned to a smaller pool of older GPU instances to reduce opportunity cost.

Auto-rollback will consume both mirrored QA signals and production telemetry but mirrored signals will be weighted conservatively (require sustained signal across 2 windows) to avoid noisy rollbacks from single anomalous mirrored batches.
risks: If sampling misconfiguration is too permissive for a few high-volume tenants, monthly mirrored cost could spike — mitigated by default conservative budgets and preflight checks.
Quarantine isolations add resource overhead; need to budget dedicated nodes which could increase infra spend if many tenants are quarantined simultaneously.
False positives in auto-rollback if mirrored QA sets are not representative; requires strong QA set curation for each canary rollout.
Operational complexity: more knobs (steady-rate, burst, budgets) increases cognitive load for SRE and customers unless Console surfaces sane defaults.
